environment: Episode 04 4K run (134 chunks), chunk S05_B/chunk-0006, 2026-10-27 13:58–14:52 local
symptom: ComfyUI aborted mid-chunk with `CUDA error: an illegal instruction was encountered` (cudaErrorIllegalInstruction, sticky) inside comfy/ldm/seedvr/color_fix.py lab_color_transfer → `Fatal Python error: Aborted`; the container restarted (restart: unless-stopped, RestartCount 1, ExitCode 0). Root then briefly started a second executor while the first (log-less) one was still alive — stopped before any dispatch.
root_cause: GPU fault of unknown origin (sporadic illegal instruction on Blackwell during the colour-transfer step; not reproduced yet) + the executor has no lost-prompt detection: after a ComfyUI restart a durable prompt_id that is absent from /history and /queue is never classified, and automatic resubmission is (correctly) forbidden, so the run hangs instead of failing loudly. Operator slip: relaunch logged to a non-existent folder and the old process looked dead but was alive.
fix_or_workaround: Root stopped the stuck executor, archived chunk-0006 state with INCIDENT.json (runs/S05_B/chunk-0006/abandoned-cuda-crash-<ts>/), verified no partial outputs, queue empty, no lock, then ran a single executor with --execute --resume (logged to technical/seedvr2-production-v004/full-run-r27-resume2.log).
prevention: Engine (T-E30): classify a dispatched prompt as LOST only when ALL hold — container StartedAt is later than the dispatch time, the prompt is absent from /history and /queue, and no output with the chunk prefix exists — then write a LOST receipt and allow exactly one automatic re-dispatch per chunk (configurable max_lost_retries in machine/recipe config), else stop loudly; add a stall watchdog (no job.json progress for N × expected seconds → alert); record GPU fault signatures from container logs into the receipt; single-executor guard (PID file + lock) so a second executor refuses to start. Operator: verify a process is dead (Get-Process by PID) and the log folder exists before relaunching.
